question.problem:
Let $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ be a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ$ given by $$ \begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ -2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned} $$ Let $Y={X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}.$ Calculate $P(1\le Y\le 5).$ *Hint: Tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,-1.2\,$ $\,0.1151\,$ $\,0.1131\,$ $\,0.1112\,$
$\,-1.1\,$ $\,0.1357\,$ $\,0.1335\,$ $\,0.1314\,$
$\,-1.0\,$ $\,0.1587\,$ $\,0.1562\,$ $\,0.1539\,$

$z$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$$\,0.03\,$
$\,-0.6\,$ $\,0.2709\,$ $\,0.2676\,$ $\,0.2643\,$
$\,-0.5\,$ $\,0.3050\,$ $\,0.3015\,$ $\,0.2981\,$
$\,-0.4\,$ $\,0.3409\,$ $\,0.3372\,$ $\,0.3336\,$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that if $X=[{X}_{1},{X}_{2}]^{T}$ is a bivariate normal random vector with mean vector $\mu $ and covariance matrix $Σ,$ given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu =[\begin{aligned}{\mu }_{1} \\ {\mu }_{2}\end{aligned}],\,Σ=[\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1}^{2} & {\sigma }_{12} \\ {\sigma }_{21} & {\sigma }_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

then the random variable $Y,$ defined as

$$
Y=a{X}_{1}+b{X}_{2}
$$

is a normally distributed random variable for all values of $a$ and $b,$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}E[Y] & =a{\mu }_{1}+b{\mu }_{2}, \\ Var[Y] & ={a}^{2}{\sigma }_{1}^{2}+{b}^{2}{\sigma }_{2}^{2}+2ab{\sigma }_{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

In our case, we have ${\mu }_{1}=5$ and ${\mu }_{2}=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[Y] & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}_{1}]+3\text{E}[{X}_{2}] \\  & ={\mu }_{1}+3\cdot {\mu }_{2} \\  & =5+3\cdot 1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we have ${\sigma }_{1}^{2}=1,{\sigma }_{2}^{2}=5,$ and ${\sigma }_{12}={\sigma }_{21}=-2.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Var[Y] & =Var[{X}_{1}+3{X}_{2}] \\  & ={1}^{2}\cdot 1+{3}^{2}\cdot 5+2\cdot 1\cdot 3\cdot (-2) \\  & =1+45-12 \\  & =34.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
Y∼N(8,34).
$$

Now, we need to compute $P(1\le Y\le 5).$ First, transform $Y$ into a standard normal random variable $Z$ by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1\le Y\le 5) & =P(\frac{1-8}{\sqrt{34}}\le Z\le \frac{5-8}{\sqrt{34}}) \\  & =P(-1.20\le Z\le -0.51)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $Φ(z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.20\le Z\le -0.51) & =P(Z\le -0.51)-P(Z<-1.20) \\  & =P(Z\le -0.51)-P(Z\le -1.20) \\  & =Φ(-0.51)-Φ(-1.20)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-1.20) & =0.1151 \\ Φ(-0.51) & =0.3050\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.20\le Z\le -0.51) & =Φ(-0.51)-Φ(-1.20) \\  & =0.3050-0.1151 \\  & =0.1899.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that

$$
P(1\le Y\le 5)=0.1899.
$$
